A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Bottlenecked Transformers and share the central information-bottleneck definitions, theorems and proofs. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on integer multiplication, polynomial evaluation and Sudoku, plus attention-entropy measurements during training (Section 5 and Appendix B).

after.justification: V3 reports original results across seven benchmarks and four pretrained backbones, training-budget and Processor ablations, and computational-overhead measurements (Section 6 and Appendices C–D).

M1.justification: V1 globally rewrites the cache every B tokens and jointly trains the backbone and Processor through the chunked sequence. V3 instead rewrites the latest newline-delimited reasoning step plus attention-selected prior entries, leaving other entries unchanged. It freezes the backbone and trains only the Processor with backpropagation truncated across reasoning-step boundaries (Section 5; Appendix B).

E1.justification: V1's generated MDP tasks—long multiplication, Horner polynomial evaluation and Sudoku, including harder difficulty ranges—are removed. V3 trains on OpenMathInstruct-2 and evaluates GSM8K, MATH, SVAMP, TheoremQA, LogiQA, Gaokao-MathQA and GSM-Hard. Coverage shifts to natural-language mathematical and logical question answering, including Chinese examination questions.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates vanilla Transformers, H2O cache pruning and restricted R-Bottlenecked Transformers. V3 evaluates SFT and SFT with 16 pause tokens against the proposed model. H2O remains cited but is no longer experimentally compared, and the restricted pruning variant disappears (the respective Table 1 comparisons).

E3.justification: V1 uses 4–16M backbones, 40 pretraining plus 40 fine-tuning epochs, validation-selected checkpoints and separate in-distribution/OOD trajectory accuracies. V3's replacement experiments use 0.6–8B backbones, one-epoch SFT baselines versus one SFT plus one Processor epoch, and greedy pass@1 evaluation with 512-token training and 2048-token response limits. Epoch-matched and parameter-sweep protocols are also introduced.

E4.justification: V1's attention-entropy versus accuracy analysis, including individual-model trajectories in Appendix B, is removed. V3 adds an epoch-matched comparison with continued SFT (Figure 3), a reconsolidation-budget sweep from k=16 to 256 (Table 2), and a Processor-size/training-duration study using four sizes over four epochs (Appendix C, Figure 4).

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V1's averaging across model variants and v3's epoch/size curves do not provide run-to-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The synthetic-task scores and entropy trajectories are replaced by benchmark, ablation and profiling results. For example, v1 Table 1 reports 69.79% overall multiplication accuracy for the 4M+2.8M model versus 52.18% for vanilla 16M. V3 Table 1 reports Llama 3.2 1B SVAMP accuracies of 44.6% for Bottlenecked, 38.0% for SFT and 41.6% for pause tokens. These differing tasks, models and training regimes do not establish a version-to-version accuracy gain.

T1.justification: The central bottleneck definitions, lemma and two Transformer theorems retain their mathematical content and proofs under renumbering. However, v1 Appendix A.4's attention-row-entropy mutual-information bound, its uniform-prior assumption and its proof are entirely removed, eliminating the formal justification for the former compression proxy.

C1.justification: V1 claims global cache transformation is necessary for generalisation and addresses limitations scaling cannot overcome, emphasizing advantages over models with up to 3.5 times more parameters. V3 reframes the contribution as selective memory consolidation/reconsolidation within auxiliary latent-space computation, emphasizing pretrained-LLM benchmark improvements of up to 6.6 percentage points. The necessity and parameter-scaling claims are dropped.

C2.justification: V1 interprets entropy trajectories as evidence of irrelevant-prefix removal and pruning failures as evidence for unrestricted memory. V3 replaces these discussions with hypotheses about long-range dependencies, Chinese distribution shift and weak next-step credit assignment. It also substantially qualifies the biological analogy, distinguishing offline consolidation from retrieval- and prediction-error-dependent reconsolidation (Sections 6–7; Appendix C).

D1.justification: V1 Appendix C provides toy-model hyperparameters, single-GPU step timings and worked MDP trajectories. V3 replaces these with dataset-subset selection, learning-rate schedules, truncation and decoding settings, pause-token embedding instructions, backbone-specific Processor counts, and training/inference memory and timing measurements. Appendix D.3 additionally discloses incompatibility with Flash Attention.

R1.justification: V1 positions the work around Transformer interpolation failures, retrieval/compression and IB-based methods such as VTrans, NVIB and QUITO-X. V3 adopts a token-mediated/residual/cache-operator taxonomy, adding substantial discussion of pause tokens, Cache Deliberation, continuous latent reasoning, activation steering and memory reconsolidation. This replaces much of the earlier literature discussion and changes the claimed research gap.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and discussion are extensively rewritten around consolidation and auxiliary latent-space computation. Related work moves from Section 7 to Section 3; the earlier theory sections are reorganized into Section 4 after new preliminaries. The title, author block and appendix organization also change.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is redrawn for recent and retrieved KV entries; multiplication heatmaps and entropy plots are removed. V3 introduces new benchmark tables, a color-coded budget-ablation table and epoch/size plots, alongside an ICLR layout. The conceptual IB diagram is retained as v3 Figure 2 from v1 Figure 4, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's acknowledged limitation of testing only tiny custom-trained models by evaluating pretrained 0.6–8B backbones and adding training-budget, selection-budget and size analyses. More bounded claims, explicit failure cases and computational-overhead disclosure substantially improve practical validation and interpretability. Controlled synthetic OOD and entropy evidence are lost, and the epoch-matched control does not match compute: Appendix D.3 reports roughly 20 times longer Processor training per epoch. Nevertheless, the stronger evidence for practical applicability and clearer claim boundaries outweigh these losses; statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
